history.dynasty: Alupa (founding inscription); rebuilt in Vijayanagara idiom
history.summary: Ancient Shaiva temple on the hills of Kadri, Mangaluru, said to be built in the 10th-11th century and converted to a complete stone structure in the 14th century (Vijayanagara style). Its earliest layer is the Buddhist Kadarika Vihara: the pedestal of the ~5-ft bronze Lokeshvara idol carries an inscription of Alupa king Kundavarma recording its installation - dated 968 CE by some sources and 1068 CE by others (Wikipedia notes the discrepancy); the image has three faces, six arms and a Dhyani-Buddha crown, and is among the oldest bronzes of South India. Two more undated bronzes - Avalokiteshvara (called Narayana) and Buddha (called Vedavyasa) - mark the Buddhist-to-Hindu transition. Legend ties the shrine to Parashurama; the 1730 text Kadli Manjunath Mahatmyam links it with the Natha panth, and a Jogi Mutt still stands above the temple. Incharge and priests are Shivalli Madhva Brahmins. CSV town 'Mangalore' is correct (Mangaluru).

name: Kadri Manjunath Temple
town_description: Mangalore (Mangaluru) is the chief port city of coastal Karnataka and headquarters of Dakshina Kannada district. It blends coastal, temple and colonial heritage, with Kadri among its oldest shrines.

travel.road: Kadri locality within Mangaluru city, on the airport road
